PullRequest.Title: Allow leaving PR comments in agents

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path from the editor action to the synchronous diff is direct, the full-file inputs and one-second budget are explicit in changed code, and the only magnitude uncertainty is how often users select very large/diverged files.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Renderer-thread CPU plus full-file line-array and diff allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Work grows with the complete PR-head file and current editor buffer, not the selected line, and is repeated for every PR-comment target selection; the explicit budget permits 1000 ms of synchronous computation per selection.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: The renderer can be blocked for up to one second, causing visible input/rendering freezes before the comment editor opens.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, selecting a feedback line did not perform a whole-file diff on this editor interaction path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Selecting a PR comment target now splits both complete file contents and invokes the synchronous default lines diff computer with maxComputationTimeMs set to 1000 before returning the target.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 147 introduces the synchronous computeDiff call, and added caller line 340 invokes it while resolving the target that the editor awaits before showing its widget.
Findings.Title: Move PR line mapping off the UI thread
Findings.Impact: With the experimental PR-comments setting enabled, choosing “Pull Request Comment” on a large or substantially diverged file can freeze the UI for up to the configured one-second diff budget before the input widget appears; each additional comment selection repeats the freeze.
Findings.Evidence: AgentFeedbackEditorInputContribution awaits getPRReviewCommentTargets before calling _show (line 536). That browser-side method reaches mapCurrentLineToPullRequestLine, where line 147 synchronously calls linesDiffComputers.getDefault().computeDiff over arrays produced from the entire remote head content and current model content, with maxComputationTimeMs: 1000. There is no worker handoff, yielding, cancellation, or cached mapping.
Findings.Recommendation: Run line mapping through the asynchronous editor worker/diff service with cancellation, or derive/cache the mapping by head SHA, path, and model version; do not execute the full-file diff synchronously in the editor interaction.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Repository tracing proves exactly one selected PR in the production caller, two concurrent requests inside refresh, then two serialized uncached requests, all awaited before widget display. Only network duration and reviewer comment count vary.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub REST requests, response bytes for all changed-file patches and full file content, and API rate-limit capacity
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The current UI selects one PR, but every attempted PR comment independently performs four GETs; cost therefore grows as 4 × the number of comment-target selections, with compare payload size also growing with the PR's changed files.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated multi-round-trip latency before the comment input appears, excessive network I/O, and avoidable GitHub API usage.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, opening the line-feedback input performed no GitHub target-resolution requests. The new compare and file-content methods also have no result cache on this path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each target lookup unconditionally refreshes the selected PR model (two concurrent GETs), then serially fetches the full compare result and full head-file content before the editor can open the input.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 329, 334, and 339 place four GitHub GETs on every newly introduced target-selection path; line 329 is the first unconditional boundary call and is awaited before any target can be returned.
Findings.Title: Reuse PR target data across comments
Findings.Impact: With PR comments enabled, every time a reviewer starts a line comment they wait for three sequential network phases (PR/reviews refresh, compare, then contents). Writing several comments on the same unchanged PR/file repeats all four GitHub GETs and can make the editor feel persistently slow on high-latency or enterprise connections.
Findings.Evidence: The editor awaits getPRReviewCommentTargets before _show. Added line 329 calls GitHubPullRequestModel.refresh(), whose implementation issues getPullRequest and getReviews in Promise.all; added lines 334 and 339 then await getChangedFiles and getFileContent serially. GitHubChangesFetcher is explicitly stateless, getFileContent directly calls GitHubApiClient, and the API client sets disableCache: true. No cache or in-flight coalescing is present for immutable base/head/path data.
Findings.Recommendation: Reuse already-loaded PR model data when fresh, and cache/coalesce compare patches and head-file content by owner/repo/base SHA/head SHA/path (invalidating naturally when head SHA changes) so repeated comments on the same revision do not refetch immutable data.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the line feedback input when PR comments are disabled, the session is not Agent Host-backed, or choose Agent Feedback from the target menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor resolves the session and local PR list, then shows the widget; no remote work must complete. A geometry read computes the context-menu anchor only when invoking the line action.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Session change count is scanned to resolve a virtual resource to a workspace resource; otherwise work is constant per invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local work only; no queue, limiter, or remote concurrency applies.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No remote cache is consulted. Existing feedback and session observables supply local state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that this path adds no expensive boundary when the feature is disabled or Agent Feedback is selected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session change lists can vary, but the scan is small relative to the remote PR path and no concrete regression mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression on the local-feedback path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose Pull Request Comment for a line in an Agent Host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The input widget is not shown until target resolution finishes: refresh PR metadata/reviews, fetch the compare response, fetch and decode the complete head file, synchronously diff complete head/current contents, and parse the selected file patch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh pull request details and reviews using two REST GETs in Promise.all
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two GETs for the one PR selected by the UI on every target-selection attempt; concurrent with each other but not with later phases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening line feedback did not refresh GitHub PR metadata or reviews.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must settle before the compare request starts and before the widget can open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the repository compare result, including patches for changed files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One uncached compare GET for the selected PR per target-selection attempt; payload scales with changed files returned by GitHub.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This editor interaction did not call the compare endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized after PR refresh and before file-content fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and base64-decode the full selected file at the PR head SHA
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One uncached contents GET for the selected file per target-selection attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This editor interaction did not fetch remote file contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized after compare; the response must be decoded before synchronous line mapping and widget display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective PR cardinality is one because the production caller passes the menu-selected PR. Network work scales as four GETs per attempted comment; CPU/allocation scales with complete remote/current file line counts and patch length, repeated for each selection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within PR refresh, two GETs run concurrently. Compare and contents requests then run in two sequential phases. Separate invocations are neither cached nor explicitly coalesced or cancelled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PR refresh has ETags only while a shared model survives, but still performs network requests. GitHubApiClient disables the renderer cache. Compare and file-content results have no cache or in-flight coalescing, even though base/head SHA/path identify immutable data. The full-file line mapping is also not cached by model version.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the editor directly awaits this method before showing the widget, all four requests and their ordering are traced, and computeDiff is synchronous over full-file arrays.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The setting is experimental/auto-enabled and actual network RTT, file size, and comments per review vary. The four-call critical path and synchronous 1000 ms diff budget are explicit, so uncertainty affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: repeated uncached network work delays every comment target selection, and synchronous whole-file diffing can block the renderer.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submit a newly authored PR line comment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget remains busy while one GitHub mutation posts or appends the comment, followed by a forced review-thread refresh; only then is the widget hidden and editor focus restored.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST a new pull-request review or execute addPullRequestReviewThread for an existing pending review
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mutation for each submitted comment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Agents Window could not post a PR line comment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The widget is busy until the mutation completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Force-refresh all review threads via GraphQL after posting
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh after each successful comment mutation; existing in-flight refresh is awaited before a forced follow-up.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No post-comment refresh existed on this new workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized after posting and awaited before the widget closes, ensuring authoritative comment state is available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One mutation plus one thread refresh per submitted comment; GraphQL response size scales with review-thread count exposed by the existing query.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Posting and refresh are strictly sequential. The thread model coalesces ordinary refreshes, while force semantics deliberately run a fresh request after any in-flight request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Review threads are held in a reference-counted observable model and polled every 60 seconds while active; forced refresh intentionally bypasses warm state after mutation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the boundary count and critical path. The refresh is an intentional consistency operation, and there is insufficient evidence that moving it off-path would preserve UX semantics.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Thread counts and network latency vary, but cardinality is bounded at two sequential operations per submission.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the post-mutation refresh is bounded and semantically tied to surfacing the newly created thread.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive, navigate, delete, or clear Agent Host feedback annotations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Annotation snapshots are decoded into the local cache; changed signatures notify editor/navigation consumers. Upsert/remove optimistically notify before dispatch. Clear sends one existing annotation-removal dispatch per feedback item while suppressing intermediate reconciliation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch annotation set/remove actions to the Agent Host channel
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per upsert/remove; clear remains one dispatch per feedback item, as before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same set/remove dispatches and per-item clear dispatch loop already existed; the diff changes local cache reconciliation and event timing rather than boundary cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatch is synchronous from the caller's perspective, but optimistic local notification now occurs first; clear suppresses per-dispatch reconciliation and emits once.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Snapshot decoding/signature work scales with annotations and feedback payload size; clear IPC scales with feedback count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Dispatches in clear are serialized in a loop. Reconciliation is suspended during that loop, preventing repeated decode/signature work for synchronous change events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A per-session optimistic cache is reconciled from authoritative snapshots. Cache, signature, loaded state, and channel references are removed when the session is deleted; the new suspension set is exited in finally and does not retain sessions after clear.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from complete backend lifecycle and event-path inspection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Annotation event frequency and payload size vary, but before/after comparison does not establish a new material performance regression; clear handling may reduce repeated work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: changed cache/signature work is comparable to prior snapshot signature construction, cleanup remains bounded, and clear now suppresses intermediate reconciliation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and navigate combined agent-feedback and PR-review comments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Consumers combine local feedback and already-loaded PR review state, build a mirrored-comment ID set, filter visibility, and group comments for editor widgets/navigation. No new remote operation is initiated by these reads.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU/allocation is linear in feedback plus loaded PR comments per recomputation; the mirrored-ID set existed previously with a narrower state predicate, so asymptotic cost is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses feedback backend cache and PR review observable state. Agent Host sessions omit raw PR comments after authoritative feedback loading to avoid duplicate representations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed filtering remains linear and does not itself initiate network work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Comment collection sizes vary, but no increased asymptotic work or new boundary was introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 29 changed files. Submitted two medium-confidence-severity findings on the new PR-comment target path: uncached four-request repetition and synchronous whole-file diffing on the renderer thread. Other touched paths either preserve boundary cardinality, reduce duplicate annotation reconciliation, or add bounded mutation refresh work required by the new workflow.
